newsitem.title: USA: Leviathan Gas, Oxy production begins.
newsitem.headline: Leviathan Gas, Oxy production begins.

text.p: Leviathan Gas Pipeline Partners LP said production has begun from the Garden Banks Block 117 2 well, offshore Louisiana, at an initial rate of 3,000 barrels of oil and 5.0 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.

The well, owned jointly with Occidental Petroleum Corp, is flowing through an adjustable choke with a stabilized flowing tubing pressure of 3,850 pounds per square inch from the Glob Alt "A" sand located at 13,500 feet. During the completion operation, the Garden Banks 117 2 well was also pre-completed in the Lentic reservoir, an oil sand located at 13,000 feet.

The Garden Banks 117 2 well is positioned 300 feet updip of the Garden Banks 117 1 well which also produces from the Glob Alt "A" reservoir. Current production from the Garden Banks 117 1 well totals 1,550 barrels of oil and 3.0 million cubic feet of gas per day.

Occidental and Leviathan each own a 50 working interests in the Garden Banks 117 lease as well as the adjacent Garden Banks Block 72. Leviathan said its interest in both leases is subject to certain reversionary rights held by Tatham Offshore Inc.

The Garden Banks 117 development has involved the successful drilling and completion of two wells and the installation of 3.5 miles of gathering lines from the subsea wellheads to the Garden Banks 72 platform.

Gas production is transported to shore on the Stingray Pipeline system, a joint venture of Leviathan and Occidental. Oil production is delivered into the Poseidon Oil Pipeline owned by Leviathan, Texaco Inc and Marathon Oil Co.
